The smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel hangs heavy in the air, a familiar scent that signals the start of another thrilling race at Interlagos.
Looking out over the bowl of Interlagos, you can feel the energy of this iconic circuit. It's a truly unique and special place.
The sun beats down relentlessly, baking the track and pushing both drivers and machines to their absolute limits.
From the Senna 'S' to Junção, the stands are packed, a testament to Brazil's undying passion for motorsport.
You can feel the history in the very asphalt here at Interlagos, a place where legends are made and dreams are shattered.
The elevation changes are dramatic, providing a natural amphitheater effect and giving fans a fantastic view of the action.
The atmosphere is electric, a carnival of speed and excitement that only Interlagos can deliver. Get ready for a wild ride!

historicalReferences: Senna's emotional victory in 1991, struggling with gearbox issues but cheered on by his adoring home crowd, remains an iconic moment at Interlagos.
Prost's calculated drive to the championship in 1986, managing his fuel and tires perfectly, showcased his strategic brilliance on this demanding circuit.
Reutemann's dominant performance in 1978, leading from start to finish, demonstrated the raw pace of the Lotus 79 on the original Interlagos layout.
Who can forget Carlos Pace's win here in 1975? A true Brazilian hero winning in front of his home crowd on this very track.
The 1993 race was another thriller, with Senna and Prost battling intensely in what would be their last season together.
In 2003, Giancarlo Fisichella took a memorable win in wet conditions, a testament to his skill and adaptability on a treacherous Interlagos circuit.

The 2008 title showdown between Hamilton and Massa was one of the most dramatic finishes in F1 history, etched into the memories of fans worldwide. Though a different layout, the emotion remains palpable.
1977 saw a dominant performance from Carlos Reutemann, showing the speed of the Ferrari on this long layout.
The 1989 race saw Nigel Mansell secure victory after a strong drive, solidifying his reputation as a formidable competitor.
The very first Brazilian Grand Prix held at Interlagos in 1973 was a spectacle, with Emerson Fittipaldi taking the win in his Lotus.
cornerCallouts: They're accelerating hard down the start/finish straight, heading towards the first challenging complex, the Senna 'S'.
Now into Curva do Sol, a long right-hander that really tests the car's balance and the driver's nerve.
Navigating the Descida do Lago now, a fast downhill section requiring precision and commitment.
The cars are now tackling the Curva do Sargento, a crucial corner for setting up the next sequence.
Here comes Ferradura, a tight left-hander that demands precise braking and smooth turn-in.
Now through the Laranja, a tricky right-hander that can easily catch drivers out.
Onto Pinheirinho now, a quick flick to the right before the final sector.
And finally, Junção, the last corner before the long run to the finish line, where overtaking is often possible.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a major factor here at Interlagos, especially on this long, demanding 7.874km layout. Expect multiple pit stops.
The long lap length means the pit lane loss is significant, so teams will be carefully calculating the optimal pit window.
Fuel management will be crucial, particularly in the early stages of the race, with such a lengthy lap to cover.
With 25 corners to navigate, finding the perfect balance between downforce and straight-line speed is key to a successful strategy.
The historic layout puts even more stress on the tires with those extra corners so expect that to be a major talking point.
A safety car period can dramatically alter the race strategy here, so teams need to be prepared to react quickly.
The high altitude can affect engine performance and fuel consumption, adding another layer of complexity to the strategic calculations.
Consider the potential for changeable weather; a perfectly planned strategy can be undone in an instant by a sudden downpour.
weatherCommentary: The clouds are gathering over the mountains, threatening to unleash a downpour on the Interlagos circuit. Rain could be on its way.
The humidity is incredibly high today, making it even more challenging for the drivers inside the cockpit.
The wind is picking up, which could affect the car's handling, particularly through the faster sections of the track.
The track temperature is soaring, which will have a significant impact on tire grip and degradation.
The unpredictable weather patterns of São Paulo can often lead to dramatic and unpredictable races at Interlagos. Be prepared for anything!
